In [basketball](Basketball "Basketball"), [points](Point_(basketball) "Point (basketball)") are accumulated through [free throws](Free_throw "Free throw") or [field goals](Field_goal_(basketball) "Field goal (basketball)").[[1]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-1) The [National Basketball Association](National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s (NBA) scoring title is awarded to the player with the highest [points per game](Points_per_game "Points per game") average in a given season. The scoring title was originally determined by total points scored through the [1968–69 season](1968%E2%80%9369_NBA_season "1968–69 NBA season"), after which points per game was used to determine the leader instead.[[2]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-scoring_title-2) The [three-point field goal](Three-point_field_goal "Three-point field goal") was introduced in the NBA at the start of the [1979–80 season](1979%E2%80%9380_NBA_season "1979–80 NBA season").[[3]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-3)[[4]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-4) To qualify for the scoring title, a player must appear in at least 58 games (out of 82). However, a player who appears in fewer than 58 games may qualify as annual scoring leader if his point total would have given him the greatest average, had he appeared in 58 games. This has been the requirement since the [2013–14 season](2013%E2%80%9314_NBA_season "2013–14 NBA season"), with requirements changing several times previously throughout history.[[5]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-ratereq-5)

[Michael Jordan](Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") has won the most scoring titles, with ten.[[7]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-jordan_bio-7) Jordan and Chamberlain are the only players to have won seven consecutive scoring titles (this was also Chamberlain's career total).[[7]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-jordan_bio-7) [George Gervin](George_Gervin "George Gervin"), [Allen Iverson](Allen_Iverson "Allen Iverson") and [Kevin Durant](Kevin_Durant "Kevin Durant") have won four scoring titles in their career,[[8]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-8) and [James Harden](James_Harden "James Harden"), [George Mikan](George_Mikan "George Mikan"), [Neil Johnston](Neil_Johnston "Neil Johnston") and [Bob McAdoo](Bob_McAdoo "Bob McAdoo") have achieved it three times. [Paul Arizin](Paul_Arizin "Paul Arizin"), [Bob Pettit](Bob_Pettit "Bob Pettit"), [Kareem Abdul-Jabbar](Kareem_Abdul-Jabbar "Kareem Abdul-Jabbar"), [Shaquille O'Neal](Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal"), [Tracy McGrady](Tracy_McGrady "Tracy McGrady"), [Kobe Bryant](Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant"), [Russell Westbrook](Russell_Westbrook "Russell Westbrook"), [Stephen Curry](Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") and [Joel Embiid](Joel_Embiid "Joel Embiid") have each won the scoring title twice. The scoring title was originally determined by total points scored through the [1968–69 season](1968%E2%80%9369_NBA_season "1968–69 NBA season"), after which points per game was used to determine the leader instead.[[2]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-scoring_title-2) The [three-point field goal](Three-point_field_goal "Three-point field goal") was introduced in the NBA at the start of the [1979–80 season](1979%E2%80%9380_NBA_season "1979–80 NBA season").[[3]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-3)[[4]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-4) To qualify for the scoring title, a player must appear in at least 58 games (out of 82). However, a player who appears in fewer than 58 games may qualify as annual scoring leader if his point total would have given him the greatest average, had he appeared in 58 games. This has been the requirement since the [2013–14 season](2013%E2%80%9314_NBA_season "2013–14 NBA season"), with requirements changing several times previously throughout history.[[5]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-ratereq-5)

[Michael Jordan](Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") has won the most scoring titles, with ten.[[7]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-jordan_bio-7) Jordan and Chamberlain are the only players to have won seven consecutive scoring titles (this was also Chamberlain's career total).[[7]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-jordan_bio-7) [George Gervin](George_Gervin "George Gervin"), [Allen Iverson](Allen_Iverson "Allen Iverson") and [Kevin Durant](Kevin_Durant "Kevin Durant") have won four scoring titles in their career,[[8]](List_of_National_Basketball_Association_annual_scoring_leaders#cite_note-8) and [James Harden](James_Harden "James Harden"), [George Mikan](George_Mikan "George Mikan"), [Neil Johnston](Neil_Johnston "Neil Johnston") and [Bob McAdoo](Bob_McAdoo "Bob McAdoo") have achieved it three times.
